The Mystery of No. 10 Dent Road.

The following was related by Mr. V.V.Gountort, who visited the editorial offices of the "Russia", yesterday and stated that he was approached by one named Prince Bakhmetoff (Tatar), who resides at No. 10 Dent Road, with a suggestion to join General Gashchin's Detachment.

Prior to consenting to join Mr. Gachtovt went, however, to the Municipal Police and informed one of the Police officers that he intended to agree to the proposition, with a view to ascertaining the recruiters and obtaining from them a document showing the "daily activities" of the III International branch in Shanghai.

A lady named Maria Pavlovna Beloglazova, and who is one of the principal and most responsible persons among the recruiters of "Whites" for Gashchin's detachment, also lives at No. 10 Dent Road.

This lady upon learning of Gostovt's "consent" gave him a list of six men recruited for the last group including a man named Lukovenko, all of whom live at No. 886 Hambury Road. Gountort was told that they were to sail on a Japanese steamer, sailing from Pootung. On November 5th at 8 p.m. he received the ticket and the money for the journey. An hour later he informed Lukovenko that he had no intentions to go to Gashchin and asked him to thank the Soviet Consulate for the money they had given him and which he could use to advantage as he needed it badly.

Lukovenko said that Gochtort was risking his life in acting in such a manner and that there is no hope that he will ever be forgiven for such an act.

The writer in conclusion expresses the hope that local authorities would take steps to fathom the mystery of this nest and says "We cannot look indifferently upon crimes which is being practiced in the face of the Local Chinese and foreign authorities."

(Sd. S. Snirvansky).

GEN. FENG REMOVING FENGTIEN TROOPS

Report that He Considers the Care of Peking His Own Affair:
Wild Tale of Mukden Recruiting Russians in Shanghai

News was received in Shanghai Chinese circles yesterday that Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang, the Christian General, has ordered the withdrawal of all Fengtien troops from Peking at once "in order that he may personally be responsible for the preservation of peace and good order" in the Capital. The reports mentioned that Marshal Feng's men have already disarmed a great number of the Fengtien soldiers, but whether this means that Feng has at last thrown in his lot with the anti-Fengtien forces is at present unknown.

The situation at the Shanghai-Nanking Railway station remained much the same yesterday as on the previous day.

A story was going round yesterday that Marshal Chang Tso-lin has been recruiting, locally, Russians who had formerly served in the Tsar's army. Marshal Sun Chuan-fang is said to have ordered a protest to be lodged at the Soviet Consulate-General (much good that would do) and to have asked that the issue of passports to Russians intending to leave Shanghai should temporarily be suspended. It all sounds very unlikely. Marshal Chang surely could get enough Russians in Manchuria.

Reports circulated yesterday that the Allied Army had commandeered a number of Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow trains and were transporting them across the Yangtze. This, however, was officially denied at the Railway Administration yesterday afternoon.

Gen. Chao Erh-hsun, former Viceroy of the Three Eastern Provinces, and Gen. Wang Shih-tsen, former Premier, in addition to Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang, are said to have offered their services as mediators in the present squabble. They have telegraphed to Marshals Chang Tso-lin, Wu Pei-fu and Sun Chuan-fang urging them to conclude an armistice and saying that they personally are prepared to visit the three leaders with a view to arriving at a peaceful under-standing. Marshal Hsiao Yao-nan, Tupan of Hupeh, who recently declared his independence of Peking, has replied that he is opposed to Fengtien and will not under any consideration enter into any peace agreement with "traitors." At least the Chinese press says so.

A Suggested Compromise

If another report in the vernacular press is correct, Marshal Chang has sent a staff officer to Hankow to meet Marshal Wu, with orders to bring up the following points, which, if agreeable to Wu, will settle the present trouble:—the overthrow of Marshal Tuan Chi-jui; the release of ex-President Tsao Kun; the restoration of the Constitution; the appointment of Gen. Wang Shih-tsen (former Premier) as President; and the surrender of Shantung by Fengtien to Marshal Wu.

Marshal Chi Hsieh-yuan, former Tuchun of Kiangsu, says the report, will be appointed Associate Commander-in-Chief of the anti-Fengtien Armies with headquarters in Nanking.

According to the Kuo Wen News Agency, Admiral Tu Shih-kuei, former Commander-in-Chief of the Chinese Fleet, has despatched his circular telegram denouncing Marshal Chang Tso-lin and instructing the commanders of the gunboats Haiyung, Haichou, Yungchi, Yungchien and Yungjui to come to Shanghai at once. 昨日流传着一则故事，称张作霖元帅正在本地招募曾效力于沙皇军队的俄罗斯人。据说孙传芳元帅已下令向苏联总领事馆提出抗议（这能有多大用处呢），并要求暂时停止向打算离开上海的俄罗斯人签发护照。这一切听起来都很不可信。张元帅肯定能在满洲招募到足够的俄罗斯人。

SHANGHAI MERCURY, WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 28, 1925.

ATTACK ON HSUCHOW STILL DELAYED.
6600
31. 10 .25.

Sun Chuan-fang Will Not Move Forward
Alone: Awaits Gesture of Allies.

WARNING ISSUED TO RUSSIANS.

It becomes increasingly evident each day that the present anti-Fengtien campaign which is being waged by the combined Chekiang and Kiangsu forces united with several Yangtze Valley provinces will culminate in the impending struggle at Hsuchowfu which is expected to begin within a few days.
Several matters are tending to delay the conflict which, it is believed, will decide the future government of the country, not the least being the uncertain attitude of Tupan Yueh Wei-chun of Honan, who, it is reported, has refused to grant his request of Marshal Wu Pei-fu, Generalissimo of the Allied anti-Fengtien Forces, to pass through Honan.
This attitude, it is believed has been caused through General Feng Yu-hsing's announcement of neutrality in the present civil strife.
Likewise it is anticipated that Dung Sz-tso, a Divisional Commander in Kiangsi, may not allow Wu to pass through Hokow, which is an important pass in Honan province.
According to the Chinese press, General Sun Chuan-fang, Tupan of Chekiang, is withholding from a further advance along the Tientsin-Pukow line because he believes that for the moment he has done his share of the offensive and that it is the duty of the Hupeh and Honan forces to give some concrete evidence of their intentions by advancing in unison with him to the attack upon Hsuchowfu.
Meanwhile Fengtien is not idle. Steady concentration of troops and supplies continues to be made at Hsuchowfu where Tupan Chang Chung-chang of Shantung, the Fengtien military leader, is giving strong indication that he is prepared to put up an extremely stubborn resistance.
The Shanghai Journal of Commerce contains information in this morning's issue upon the point, explaining that the Fengtien Army has been massed at this point and will prove a difficult obstacle for the Wu Pei-fu forces to surmount in their march upon Peking if such be their intention.
General Sun Chuan-fang has clearly stated that he will not attack Hsuchowfu unless he receives the assistance also of the Hupeh Army.
The Chekiang General's attitude is quite sound for to attempt to march alone to the attack upon the Fengtien stronghold would be practically a suicidal policy.
Yesterday we reported that General Sun had telegraphed to the local authorities of the Shanghai-Nanking Railway requesting that a couple of hundred railway coaches and wagons in addition to ten engines be transferred across the Yangtze to Pukow for use of his army in the advance upon Hsuchow.
That request the S.-N. R. Administration was not able to accede to.
The proposal was quite out of the question and both the British and Chinese Corporations strongly opposed such a course.
Perhaps it were just as well. The military have given every justification in the past for such refusal for they are notorious bunglers when it comes to administrating a railway service.
If General Sun Chuan-fang desires at a later date to make a sudden and unanimous attack upon Hsuchowfu he were better advised to do so in the manner in which he has found reliable and successful in the past—on foot.
The Chekiang leader made a reputation for himself during the last provincial war when he covered tremendous distances on foot with his Fukien troops in the march upon Hangchow.
Moreover the distance separating the two armies at present is not by any means repellant. From Pengpu, where General Sun is at present, to Hsuchowfu is but a distance of 175 kilometres or approximately 105 miles and greater distances than that have been covered by General Sun's men before.
Then there is another point which inclines towards the belief that General Sun is merely awaiting some definite information from Hupeh and Honan and not for adequate means of transportation. If the Chekiang Commander where so short of railway rolling stock it is not likely that he would overlook the locomotives and coaches which are now maintaining a passenger service between Pukow and Pengpu.
Marshal Chang Tso-lin is by no means perturbed over the present situation, the Chinese press states. He is devoting his whole force to the protection of Hsuchowfu, Chihli and Shantung.
A number of Russian troops have been despatched to Kia Ker (the reported scene of Sunday's battle in which the anti-Fengtien forces are said to have suffered minor reverses). Cannons and electric netting have been placed on both boundaries of Kia Ker.

Russians Are Warned.

In view of the fact that Chang Tso-lin has detailed agents to Shanghai to recruit Russian "Whites" and that those "Whites" of military knowledge are taken on for military purposes while others are employed to act as spies in the interior to detect war activities of the enemy, Sun Chuan-fang has instructed the local Commissioner for Foreign Affairs to notify the Russian Consul in Shanghai to warn Russians here not to proceed into the interior on any pretext whatsoever at the present time.
In the meantime military and police authorities in various places have been instructed to keep a close watch on the activities of Russians.
Yesterday Yen Tsung-yang, Commander of the Woosung and Shanghai Martial Law Force also received a telegram from General Sun instructing him to warn all soldiers stationed along the railway line to keep a watch on the activities of Russians. Commander Yen yesterday conveyed the instructions to Kiang Ching-chen, Chief of the Woosung and Shanghai Constabulary who has in turn instructed his subordinates to keep watch on the activities of Russians whilst on duty.
Soldiers now stationed at Lunghwa are to be transferred within one or two days to various coastal regions in Chuso, Nanwei as a result of a report stating that Pei Shih-cheng, Commander of the Naval Squadron in Chefoo, will bring his forces to attack various places along the coast of Kiangsu and Chekiang.
General Sun Chuan-fang sent a number of Lu Shang-ting's soldiers to Shanghai and also directed the Commander of the Kiangsu Salt Smuggling Prevention Force to co-operate with Colonel Liu Sz-ling, Commander of the 6th Regiment, 2nd Division, Chekiang Army, in adopting precautionary measures at Beh Loong Kong, Chuso, Nanwei and Paoshan districts.
According to the Sinwanpao of this morning's issue, it is reported that as result of the opening of the Tariff Conference on Monday, Marshal Wu Pei-fu has decided to proceed to Nanking, to be followed shortly after by the 25th Division of General Chen Chia-mu's army which will be transported by six gunboats.
Also, states the same paper, General Feng Yu-hsiang has warned Tupan Yueh Wei-chun of Honan against being drawn into the present turmoil.

Ex Police Chief Sai's.

Tsen Chien, ex-Governor of Kiangsu who has been living in a refuge in the Settlement after he made a good escape from Nanking, accompanied by his family left here this morning at 8 o'clock for Dairen on board the D. K. K. Sakaki Maru.
Colonel Chiang Tsz-ying, ex-Chief of the Chinese Constabulary who was once taken into custody by the Chekiang forces but recently escaped took the same vessel to go to Tsingtao whence it is said he will proceed to Tsinan.

Tientsin, Oct. 27.

General Yueh Wei-chun of Honan has made an announcement through his circular telegram, expressing his thanks to General Li Ching-lin, Tupan of Chihli, for the friendly attitude shown to Honan by the troops of General Li, and stating that Honan is determined to act in co-operation with Fengtien to maintain the general situation.

In the same telegram, General Yueh also declares that he assumes the full responsibility to expel Hupeh troops in case they invade his province, Honan.—Eastern News Agency.

Peking, Oct. 27.

It is reliably reported that General Sun Chuan-fang's forces are only advancing very slowly on Hsuchowfu owing to the absence of rolling-stock, most of which, it is reported, was taken northwards by the Fengtien troops, also owing to the damages to the line.
The Fengtien forces also are reported to be taking longer than was expected over the concentration at Hsuchowfu.
Hence, well-informed quarters do not expect serious fighting to take place for a week.
The Government is reported to have wired to Marshal Chang Tso-lin and Generals Feng Yu-hsiang and Yueh Wei-chun, asking them to send two delegates each to Peking to discuss the situation.
The Chairman of the Military Rehabilitation Commission, Mr. Wang Shih-chen, and the Chairman of the Tsanchengyuen, Mr. Chao Erh-hsun, wired this evening to Marshal Chang Tso-lin and Marshal Wu Pei-fu urging a compromise between them, being prepared if necessary to visit Hankow and Mukden respectively.—Reuter's Pacific Service.

Panic in Tsingtao.

Tsingtao, Oct. 27.

The Chinese fleet here, belonging to the Fengtien faction, with a view to attacking Haichow, has started to commandeer native junks here, thereby causing a great panic in Tsingtao.—Eastern News Agency.

Changchun, Oct. 27.

The 38th Regiment of the 15th Brigade of Heilungkiang Army, including 85 officers and 1,035 non coms and soldiers, with 4 field pieces, 40 cases of ammunition, 138 horses as well as other military supplies passed Changchun at 10 a.m. to-day for Mukden.—Eastern News Agency.

《上海泰晤士报》，1925年10月28日，星期三。

进攻徐州仍被推迟。
6600
31. 10 .25.

孙传芳不愿单独进军：等待盟友姿态。

向俄国人发出警告。

日益明显的是，由浙江和江苏部队联合长江流域数省正在进行的当前反奉系战役，将以即将在徐州府爆发的斗争为高潮，预计该战斗将在几天内开始。
有几个因素倾向于推迟这场被认为将决定国家未来政府的冲突，其中最重要的是河南督军岳维春态度不明，据报道，他拒绝了反奉联军总司令吴佩孚元帅提出的借道河南的请求。
人们认为，这种态度是由于冯玉祥将军宣布在当前内战中保持中立所致。
同样，预计江西的一位师长董师佐（音译）可能不会允许吴佩孚通过河口，这是河南省的一个重要关口。
据中文报刊报道，浙江督军孙传芳将军正暂缓沿津浦线进一步推进，因为他认为目前他已尽到了进攻的分内之责，湖北和河南部队有义务通过与他在进攻徐州府的行动中保持一致推进，来提供其意图的具体证据。
与此同时，奉系并非无所作为。在徐州府，部队和物资的持续集结仍在进行，山东督军、奉系军事领袖张宗昌强烈暗示他准备进行极其顽强的抵抗。
《商业日报》在今晨的刊文中就此提供了信息，解释说奉军已在此处集结，如果吴佩孚部队有意进军北京，这将被证明是一个难以克服的障碍。
孙传芳将军已明确表示，除非得到湖北军队的援助，否则他不会进攻徐州府。
这位浙江将军的态度十分明智，因为试图单独进军攻击奉系 stronghold（据点）实际上是一种自杀政策。
昨天我们报道说，孙将军已致电沪宁铁路地方当局，请求除了十台机车外，再调拨几百节铁路客车和货车越过长江至浦口，供其军队在进攻徐州时使用。
沪宁铁路管理局无法同意这一请求。
该提议完全不可行，英方和中方公司均强烈反对这种做法。
也许这样也好。军方过去为这种拒绝提供了充分的理由，因为在管理铁路服务方面，他们是出了名的笨手笨脚者。
如果孙传芳将军希望日后对徐州府发动突然且一致的进攻，最好还是采用他过去发现可靠且成功的方式——步行。
这位浙江领导人在上次省战中为自己赢得了声誉，当时他率领福建部队在进军杭州的过程中徒步覆盖了巨大的距离。
此外，目前两军之间的距离绝非令人望而却步。从孙将军目前所在的蚌埠到徐州府，距离仅为175公里，或约105英里，而孙将军的部下以前曾覆盖过比这更长的距离。
还有另一点使人倾向于相信，孙将军只是在等待来自湖北和河南的一些确切消息，而不是在等待足够的运输工具。如果这位浙江指挥官真的如此缺乏铁路车辆，他不太可能忽视目前正在浦口和蚌埠之间维持客运服务的机车和车厢。
中文报刊称，张作霖元帅对目前的局势毫不担忧。他正全力致力于保护徐州府、直隶和山东。
一批俄国士兵已被派往贾克尔（Kia Ker，据称是周日战斗的发生地，反奉军据说在那里遭受了轻微挫折）。贾克尔的两端边界均已部署了大炮和电网。

警告俄国人。

鉴于张作霖已派遣特工到上海招募俄国“白俄”，且那些具备军事知识的“白俄”被录用用于军事目的，而其他人则被雇用在内地充当间谍以侦测敌方的战争活动，孙传芳已指示当地外交特派员通知驻上海俄国领事，警告在沪俄人目前不得以任何借口进入内地。
同时，各地军事和警察当局已接到指令，密切监视俄国人的活动。
昨天，淞沪戒严司令官严重阳将军也收到孙将军的电报，指示他警告所有驻扎在铁路沿线的士兵监视俄国人的活动。严司令昨天将此指示传达给淞沪警察厅厅长蒋敬臣，后者又指示其下属在执勤时监视俄国人的活动。
由于有报告称烟台海军舰队司令毕世澄（音译）将率部进攻江苏和浙江沿海各地，目前驻扎在龙华的士兵将在一两天内调往柘林、南汇等沿海地区。
孙传芳将军派遣了一些卢香亭的士兵到上海，并指示江苏缉私统领与浙军第二师第六团团长刘士林上校合作，在白龙港、柘林、南汇和宝山地区采取预防措施。
据今晨《新闻报》报道，由于周一关税会议的召开，吴佩孚元帅决定前往南京，随后陈嘉谟将军的第二十五师将由六艘炮艇运送紧随其后。
该报还称，冯玉祥将军已警告河南督军岳维春不要卷入当前的混乱局面。

前警察局长赛氏等人。

前任江苏督军岑春煊在从南京成功逃脱后一直居住在租界内的避难所，今晨8时携家人乘坐大连汽船会社（D. K. K.）的“榊丸”号（Sakaki Maru）离开此处前往大连。
前任中国警察厅长蒋志英上校曾被浙江部队拘留但最近逃脱，他乘坐同一艘船只前往青岛，据说他将从那里前往济南。

天津，10月27日。

河南督军岳维春将军通过通电路发表声明，感谢直隶督军李景林将军对其部队向河南表示的友好态度，并声明河南决心与奉系合作以维持大局。
在同一份电报中，岳将军还声明，如果湖北军队入侵其省份河南，他将承担驱逐他们的全部责任。——东方通讯社。

北京，10月27日。

据可靠消息报道，由于缺乏车辆（据报道大部分车辆已被奉军北运），以及线路受损，孙传芳将军的部队向徐州府的推进非常缓慢。
据报道，奉军在徐州府的集结所用时间也比预期的要长。
因此，消息灵通人士预计一周内不会发生激烈战斗。
据报道，政府已致电张作霖元帅以及冯玉祥和岳维春将军，要求他们各派两名代表到北京讨论局势。
军事善后委员会主席王士珍先生和参政院院长赵尔巽先生今晚致电张作霖元帅和吴佩孚元帅，敦促双方妥协，并表示如有必要，准备分别前往汉口和沈阳。——路透社太平洋分社。

青岛恐慌。

青岛，10月27日。
此处属于奉系的中國舰队为了进攻海州，已开始征用当地的民船，从而在青岛引起了极大恐慌。——东方通讯社。

长春，10月27日。
黑龙江陆军第十五旅第三十八团，包括85名军官和1,035名士官及士兵，携带4门野战炮、40箱弹药、138匹马以及其他军用物资，于今天上午10时经过长春前往沈阳。——东方通讯社。

"Russ'."
31/10/25.

We have been refugees for five years. During that time of destitute living, shame and humiliation I did not consider myself as Ataman nor you as Cossacks.
Now, I am once more your lawful Ataman because I have ceased to be a refugee and am working hand in hand with the true son of our Country, General Gushchin.
I am again in your midst, leading and marching my countrymen and say to you all:-
Enough of listening to the ravings of the followers of Nicholas and Kirill, who are selling Russia to foreigners.
Enough of serving the British, Japanese, French and Americans. We now know what sort of friends they are. It is time for us to understand that foreigners are our enemies and those Russians like Michneff and others who serve them are traitors. It is quite clear that Chang Tso Lin is a slave to Japan, and Michneff to Chang Tso Lin, which means that he is sharpening the knife against his Mother-country. I your Ataman have found a door which is opening, an honest and honourable way home. This door is the Division of General Gushchin who is prepared to face all those who threaten Russia.
I promise to start you on this way if you so desire, and you will return home not as amnestied criminals, but carrying your heads proudly as sons of their Mother-country who have earned this right.
Cossacks do not think that I am personally, for bettering my position, interested in seeing you in General Gushchin's detachment. I am calling you because my duty before you as your Ataman tells me to point out to you a real honest way out, and also because now the time has come to follow same, in time it may be too late.

October 17, 1925.
(Signed)
S. P. Ivanoff-Rinoff
Ataman of the Siberian Cossack Army.

(Ed. Note: The original is kept in my office).

“俄罗斯人。”
31/10/25.

我们已成为难民五年了。在那段贫困、羞耻和屈辱的生活中，我并不视自己为阿塔曼（Ataman，哥萨克首领），也不视你们为哥萨克。
现在，我再次成为你们合法的阿塔曼，因为我不再是难民，而是与我们国家真正的儿子古谢钦将军携手工作。
我再次回到你们中间，带领我的同胞行进，并对你们所有人说：
不要再听信尼古拉和基里尔的追随者的胡言乱语，他们正在将俄罗斯出卖给外国人。
不要再为英国人、日本人、法国人和美国人效力。我们现在知道他们是怎样的朋友。是时候让我们明白，外国人是我们的敌人，而那些像米赫涅夫（Michneff）及其他为他们服务的俄国人是叛徒。很明显，张作霖是日本的奴隶，而米赫涅夫是张作霖的奴隶，这意味着他正在磨刀霍霍指向他的祖国。我，你们的阿塔曼，已经找到了一扇正在打开的门，一条诚实且光荣的回家之路。这扇门就是古谢钦将军的师，他准备面对所有威胁俄罗斯的人。
如果你们愿意，我承诺带你们走上这条路，你们将不再是作为被赦免的罪犯回家，而是作为赢得这一权利的祖国之子，自豪地昂着头回家。
哥萨克们不要认为我是出于个人改善地位的考虑，才希望看到你们加入古谢钦将军的分队。我召唤你们，是因为我作为你们的阿塔曼对你们负有责任，这告诉我必须为你们指出一条真正诚实的出路，同时也因为现在是遵循这条道路的时候了，否则可能就太晚了。

1925年10月17日。
（签名）
S. P. Ivanoff-Rinoff
西伯利亚哥萨克军阿塔曼。

（编者注：原件存于我的办公室）。

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL

Shanghai, October 10, 1924

Sir,

Between two or three hundred Russians together
with Chinese soldiers are now encamped at Loyang, Honan.
Of this number about sixty were recruited in Shanghai, the
remainder were assembled in Mukden, Harbin and Tientsin.
The Russian soldiers are under the command of Colonel
Tutchin, who was deported from Shanghai in June 1925.

Belosludtseff who is one of the men concerned
in the recruiting here was formerly Sergeant-Major
under General Anissimoff on board the S. S. "Mongugai".

Your Obedient Servant,

D. C. I.

Commissioner of Police.

recruited locally and in other places in China for a
regiment which was being formed at Kaifeng in Honan

three hundred strong, is constantly increasing and
comprises two batteries of artillery of six guns each.

come from Mongolia were transferred to the Military
Headquarters of the above mentioned place together with
a great quantity of ammunition. The Commander is a
Chinese General bearing the name of Kung Jung (Chinese

Sir,

I beg to inform you that Beloslutzeff, who is a representative of the Russian Ambassador at Peking, by telling false-hoods recruited my partner and myself ( my partner being Hady Halieff ) into the Chinese Army which is lying at Loyang.

Beloslutzeff informed us that he was employing Russians for service in Karahan's Guard. We gave our consent and were enlisted as guards.

On the 10th. inst. at 2. a.m. they brought us on the ship "Kiang Kwang" and settled there just five minutes before its departure.

In the morning about 5 o'clock I discovered that our ship was not going to Tientsin but to Hankow and, after my question as to why it was going there, a Communist fellow who accompanied us, explained to me that we were going there because that was the safest way to reach Peking as the Tientsin-Pukow Railway was occupied by Marshal Chang-Tso-Lin.

On the 14th. inst. we reached Hankow and there three more Russians joined us.

On the 15th. inst. in the morning we reached Cheng-chow and there two Russians met us. One of them was Commissioner Zvereff. They brought us to Loyang where the headquarters of military forces are situated..

（当时我患有痢疾），我说由于健康状况我无法服役，我的目的是住在北京并恢复健康。接着我的搭档也说他没有意向去服兵役。

随后，那位委员知道我们没钱，便笑着说：“好吧，你们可以自费去北京，试着在大使馆找份工作。”我们回答说我们没有钱。“那你们就去团里吧，”他回答道，然后走了出去。

鉴于我们两人表现出不满情绪，他命令两名俄国间谍监视我们，他们在白天一直盯着我们。尽管如此，通过在士兵和他们的营房之间走动，我们了解到那里部署了两个炮兵连，每连六门火炮，并且还有大约两三百名俄国人。

在我们到达的前一天，他们刚刚接收了大量弹药和约四百匹来自蒙古的马匹。

这支军队的总司令是中国将军孔江（Kung-Jang），参谋长是俄国将军古申（Guschin）。

据我了解，他们每天都在等待来自中国各地和蒙古的俄国人，并准备与张作霖以及英国和其他大帝国作战。每天晚上，他们都向士兵宣读，他们的职责是推翻帝国主义的暴政。

to have drinks with us and they gladly consented. After a lot of
drinks we went to bed. Seeing them sleeping soundly about 4 a.m.
we escaped from our house to the railway station which was about
three miles away. There we caught a train and set off to Cheng-Chow.
From Cheng-Chow we went to Peking and reached that city on
the 18th.. After a few hours we went to the Russian Embassy asking
there for a job and for help as poor Russians.
Karahan's Secretary, looking at Halieff and myself suspiciously, tried to persuade us that they had no job for us, but that
they could only help us by giving us Soviet pass-ports and sending
us to Russia. Then he gave me an application form but said to Halieff,
"If you wish, you can stay at our house until we can find
something for you."
They kept him one day at the Embassy and after asking him
many questions, on the next morning said that that they could not
do anything for him.
In addition I may say that there is no real force in the
Russian Embassy, all the servants being Chinese except the
secretaries who are Russians and Jews.
I arrived in Shanghai by train from Peking via Tientsin and
Nanking at 10.30 p.m. September 23rd. 1925.
Yours Obediently,
B. Pushkin.

和我们一起喝酒，他们欣然同意。喝了很多酒之后，我们就去睡觉了。看到他们在凌晨4点左右熟睡，我们从住所逃到了大约三英里外的火车站。在那里我们搭上一列火车前往郑州。从郑州我们去了北京，并于18日抵达该市。几个小时后，我们前往俄国大使馆，以贫困俄国人的身份请求工作和帮助。

卡拉汉的秘书怀疑地看着哈利耶夫和我，试图说服我们说他们没有工作可以提供给我们，但他们可以通过给我们苏联护照并将我们送往俄国来提供帮助。然后他给了我一份申请表，但对哈利耶夫说：“如果你愿意，你可以住在我们的寓所，直到我们为你找到事情做。”

他们在大使馆留了他一天，问了他许多问题后，第二天早上说他们无法为他做任何事。

此外，我还要说明，俄国大使馆内没有真正的武力，所有的仆役都是中国人，除了秘书是俄国人和犹太人。

我于1925年9月23日晚上10点30分，乘火车经天津和南京从北京抵达上海。

您恭顺的，
B. 普希金。

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL September 11 1925

REPORT ON Communist activities.

Made by D. S. I. Yorke. Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

Further to my attached report of
9-9-25. Temporary Constable Pushkin reported to the Communists
Agents at No. 19 Dent Road at 10am. 10-9-25. and received
instructions to take his belongings to that address at 2pm. when he,
together with Hadi Habief, would be photographed and then proceed to
a secret address there to await the departure of a steamer for
Tientsin. Pushkin understood that they would leave Shanghai in the
early hours of 11-9-25. It was found necessary for Habief to
accompany Pushkin in order to avoid suspicion being aroused against
Pushkin. Reports from Pushkin will be addressed to a fictitious
" G. Parker ", No. 7 Robinson Gardens and will be signed " Basil
Trapeznikoff ". Arrangements have been made to collect these letters
Pushkin was, after the necessary permission had been obtained,
furnished with the sum of $200. in case of an emergency arising
which necessitates a quick return to Shanghai.

D. C. I. (批：Subsequently)
(批：11/9)

I am, Sir,
Your obediently,
(签名：Yorke)
D. S. I.

由特别侦查员约克（D. S. I. Yorke）撰写。经刑事侦缉处处长转呈。

先生：

继我附上的1925年9月9日报告之后。临时警员普希金于1925年9月10日上午10点向登特路19号的共产党代理人报到，并接受指示，要求他在下午2点将行李带到该地址，届时他将与哈迪·哈比耶夫（Hadi Habief）一起拍照，然后前往那里的一个秘密地址，等待前往天津的轮船出发。普希金得知他们将在1925年9月11日凌晨离开上海。为了避免引起对普希金的怀疑，哈比耶夫有必要陪同普希金。普希金的报告将寄给罗宾逊花园7号虚构的“G. Parker”，并署名“巴西尔·特拉佩兹尼科夫（Basil Trapeznikoff）”。已安排收取这些信件。
在获得必要许可后，普希金获得了200美元，以备出现需要迅速返回上海的紧急情况之需。

D. C. I. （批注：随后）

Made by D. S. I. Yorke. Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.
Sir,
I beg to report that, at 10 a.m. 9/9/25,
a Russian of Tartar extraction named Hadi Habieff came to Hongkew
Station and reported that certain Russian Communists in the
Wayside District were recruiting local Russians to serve as a
guard for the Soviet Embassy in Peking and that he, Habieff had
been asked to join this guard.
Habieff was requested by me to join up the guard and proceed to
Peking if necessary, at the same time keeping the Police in
Shanghai informed by letter of his movements, and developments in
Peking. He refused to adopt this course firstly, because he is
employed in the British-American Tobacco Co. and secondly because
he does not wish, on any account, to have dealings with the
Soviet as they massacred his father and brothers in Ufa.
The services of T. P. C. 278 Pushkin were
enlisted and he, went together with Habieff dressing in old clothes
and assuming a dirty and dishevelled appearance to No. 19 Dent
Road, the headquarters of the Communists engaged in recruiting
and offered his services to them.

The house No. 19 is rented by an old Jewish woman named
Tannenbaum who is known to D. S. Repas. The upstairs front room
is occupied by one, Belosludtseff, who states he is acting as
Secretary to one, Hairulla Abdulgalomoff. The latter is the
person actually entrusted with the enlisting of the guard. He
was not present when Pushkin visited No. 19 Dent Road to offer

先生：
谨此报告，1925年9月9日上午10点，一名鞑靼裔俄国人哈迪·哈比耶夫（Hadi Habieff）来到虹口巡捕房报告称，西区（Wayside District）的某些俄国共产党人正在招募本地俄国人，担任北京苏联大使馆的卫兵，而他，哈比耶夫，已被邀请加入该卫队。

我要求哈比耶夫加入卫队，如有必要则前往北京，同时通过信件向上海警方通报他的行踪以及北京的事态发展。他拒绝采取这一做法，首先，因为他受雇于英美烟草公司；其次，因为他无论如何都不愿与苏维埃打交道，因为他们在乌法屠杀了他的父亲和兄弟。

于是征用了特务警察278号普希金的服务，他与哈比耶夫一起，穿着旧衣服，装作肮脏凌乱的样子，前往登特路19号，即从事招募工作的共产党人的总部，并向他们提供服务。
